teaser: Every article read a second time as facts, names and sources, joined under one grammar; the brief, the method and ten predictions, before the run.
core_idea: The newsroom's 187 article graphs are islands, 48 labels shared between articles and 401 of 672 tags used once, so every article is read a second time from the bottom up as its claims, names, concepts, sources and dates, each anchored to a quote, under one grammar whose edges are verbs with inverses; the layers above, gravity, clusters, peaks and a two-way cut, are then computed from the join and scored against the editor's hand-drawn layers, with ten numbered predictions published before any article is read so the second article can say which held.

nodes.label: The graphs are islands
nodes.summary: 2,348 nodes in 187 graphs; 48 labels appear in more than one article; 401 of 672 tags used once.

nodes.label: The owner's memo
nodes.summary: Read every article bottom-up as facts, hypotheses, data, names and sources; let the dimensions emerge; find the peaks; draw it.

nodes.label: One grammar, five rules
nodes.summary: Every edge a verb with a named inverse, no generic association, data not meaning in properties, supersede never delete, render the answer.

nodes.label: A new dimension where the words change
nodes.summary: A layer with its own types and verbs; the same vocabulary further away is the same dimension at less resolution.

nodes.label: One file beside every article
nodes.summary: Claims with kind, section and verbatim quote; edges; names; concepts; dated sources; dates.

nodes.label: The validator
nodes.summary: Finds every quote in the twin, refuses unknown kinds and verbs, the banned edge, the em-dash and the ladder word.

nodes.label: Registries seeded, not empty
nodes.summary: 75 concepts from the controlled subjects and the house terms; 137 names from a scan of proper nouns and cited sites.

nodes.label: The worked example
nodes.summary: Every link points back as 25 claims, 17 edges, two names, six concepts, written first and passing.

nodes.label: The run, in order
nodes.summary: This article first, then readers in batches, then the merge, then a deterministic derivation, then the second article.

nodes.label: Gravity, clusters, peaks
nodes.summary: Queries over the join: ids in two or more articles, clusters of concepts, the nodes that bridge them.

nodes.label: The editor's layers as the control
nodes.summary: Six topics, five desks, 44 subjects, eleven series, the sections and personas, drawn by hand, scored against.

nodes.label: The two-way cut
nodes.summary: A force layout cut into two lobes, after rUv's map of his own work, attributed to the owner's memory.

nodes.label: Ten predictions
nodes.summary: 3,500 to 5,500 claims; 300 shared ids; five dimensions and one unlisted; six to nine clusters; the peaks; what will go wrong.

nodes.label: The standing brief
nodes.summary: The same text as a README beside the files, read first by every later run, with its own expectations added.

nodes.label: The misses are the finding
nodes.summary: Which predictions hold and which miss is what the second article is about.

quotes.text: The site says a node has no meaning of its own and takes it from what it is connected to, and its own article graphs connect to almost nothing outside their article.
quotes.why: The finding the brief starts from, in one sentence.

quotes.text: A prediction that holds says the method is understood.
quotes.why: Why the predictions are published before the run.
